wins.text: Q4 revenue of $13.7B came in at the high end of guidance, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of beating guidance
DCAI revenue of $4.7B grew 15% sequentially, the fastest sequential growth this decade, driven by strong traditional server demand
Custom ASIC business grew more than 50% in 2025, 26% sequentially, reaching an annualized revenue run rate greater than $1B in Q4
Non-GAAP EPS of $0.15 vs. guidance of $0.08, driven by higher revenue, stronger gross margins, and spending discipline; full-year non-GAAP OpEx down 15% YoY to $16.5B

Delivered 3 Core Ultra Series 3 SKUs on Intel 18A ahead of commitment of one; Series 3 powering over 200 notebook designs at CES with up to 27 hours battery life and 70% gen-on-gen graphics improvement

risks.text: Q1 2026 revenue guided to $11.7B–$12.7B (midpoint $12.2B), below seasonal norms, with gross margin guided down to ~34.5% and breakeven EPS, driven by acute internal supply constraints
Supply constraints meaningfully limited Q4 revenue capture and are most acute in Q1 2026; finished goods inventory depleted to ~40% of peak levels, leaving the business hand-to-mouth on fab output
Intel 18A ramp is dilutive to corporate gross margins; Panther Lake cost structure still below corporate average and represents a larger mix in Q1, pressuring margins further
Rising DRAM, NAND, and substrate pricing due to AI infrastructure demand could limit client revenue opportunity in 2026
External foundry revenue remains nascent at $222M in Q4; meaningful 14A wafer revenue from external customers not expected until risk production in late 2027 and volume production in 2028

guidance_items.detail: Q1 2026 guided to $11.7B–$12.7B (midpoint $12.2B), at the low end of seasonal; supply constraints most acute in Q1 with improvement expected from Q2 onward
Q1 non-GAAP gross margin guided to ~34.5%, down from 37.9% in Q4, due to lower revenue, increased 18A volumes, and product mix
Q1 non-GAAP EPS guided to approximately breakeven vs. $0.15 in Q4
2026 CapEx now planned flat to slightly down vs. prior guidance of down; more weighted to H1, with increased tool spending to address supply shortfall
2026 non-GAAP OpEx targeted at $16B; positive adjusted free cash flow expected for full year 2026; $2.5B in debt maturities to be retired

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Why Intel is in a severe finished-goods inventory shortage despite owning its own fabs and having $11.6B of total inventory on the balance sheet
Competitive server CPU market share risk from x86 rival and ARM-based alternatives during Intel's supply-constrained period
Specific timing and revenue scale targets needed to declare the external foundry business a success
